Verdict

No confirmed signs of malicious supply-chain compromise. Overall risk: **info**.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • The provided extracted text shows no evidence of .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, or setup.py-based automatic execution.
  • .github/workflows/release.yml appears to perform normal wheel/sdist builds and publication to PyPI/GitHub Releases. Copying dist/*.whl and dist/*.tar.gz is consistent with a normal release workflow.
  • The dynamic import in qmc.py loads the Rust extension module (nonebot_plugin_kuwo._qmc_rs) when used. Based on the provided evidence, this is not an install-time or interpreter-start malicious execution path.
  • Normal plugin commands / NoneBot runtime behavior are user- or application-triggered and were not classified as malicious automatic execution.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • No evidence was found of broad credential discovery, .env/SSH/cloud/kube/CI token harvesting, or broad environment-variable collection.
  • Network indicators appear to be Kuwo music service API/image/media URLs and PyPI lockfile URLs. No evidence links them to credential exfiltration or attacker-controlled C2.
  • Pre-scan archive/staging hits are explainable as release artifact collection in the GitHub Actions workflow and sdist URLs in uv.lock; no evidence of archiving harvested files or exfiltrating them was found.
  • No evidence of persistence mechanisms such as cron, systemd, launch agents, or shell profile modification was found.
  • No evidence of Kubernetes, Docker socket, cloud metadata, GitHub Actions token theft, or workflow injection for lateral movement was found.
  • The Rust/Python decryption routines and test .mflac file match the documented Kuwo/QMC music-file decryption feature. No additional evidence indicates a hidden malicious payload or staged loader.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • The Rust/PyO3 native extension source (src/lib.rs, src/qmc.rs) matches the README/PKG-INFO description of .mflac decryption functionality.
  • The high-entropy test .mflac file appears expected for the relevant tests and documented feature; no evidence indicates it is a hidden payload.
  • Numerous files.pythonhosted.org URLs in uv.lock appear to be dependency lock metadata and are not, by themselves, evidence of malicious download or exfiltration.
  • Based on the current input, no typosquatting, sudden dependency insertion, wheel/sdist mismatch, or unexplained native binary was confirmed.

Further Verification Needed

  • The provided text corpus does not include the full contents of pyproject.toml, nonebot_plugin_kuwo/__init__.py, data_source.py, and other files, so automatic registration or import-time side effects were not fully verified.
  • The compiled native binary (_qmc_rs) in actual PyPI wheels should be compared against the sdist source separately.
  • Large/binary test files cannot be fully validated from static text alone; if needed, verify their hashes and whether they match known test samples.
